title: Protect collection tree integrity and import/export round trips
description:
Make every collection mutation transactional and validate the full resulting graph before commit. Reject duplicate identifiers, missing parents, cycles, self-parenting, moves into descendants, and request references to nonexistent collections. A failed move/import/delete must leave the previous tree unchanged; deleting a collection must explicitly cascade or relocate descendants and requests rather than orphaning them.

Introduce a recursive versioned export that preserves nested collections, ordering, requests, variable scopes, and authentication references while applying the secret-redaction policy. Import into a staging model, validate identifiers and references, surface a useful conflict report, and commit only after the whole document passes. Preserve compatibility with supported legacy exports through an explicit migration path.

Round-trip tests must demonstrate semantic equality for deeply nested trees and prove that malformed or adversarial input cannot delete unrelated data.

checklist.text: Document graph invariants for IDs, parents, ordering, request ownership, and deletion behavior
Stage and validate create, rename, move, reorder, and delete mutations before an atomic commit
Reject cycles, self/descendant moves, duplicate IDs, missing parents, and orphaned request references
Define and implement explicit cascade or relocation behavior for collection deletion
Create a recursive versioned export preserving hierarchy, order, requests, variables, and redacted auth
Validate imports in staging and report conflicts without partially mutating stored data
Test deep round trips, legacy migration, malformed graphs, failed transactions, and unrelated-data preservation
